Overview

Halo UI

The open-source design system and React component library that powers every Lumen Labs product.

stable

Halo UI is the shared design language behind Aperture (our analytics suite), Relay (our messaging platform), and the Lumen Labs marketing site. It ships 38 accessible components, 412 design tokens, and a themeable runtime that weighs 11.4 kB gzipped for the core layer.

Everything you read in these docs is written in MDX — Markdown prose interleaved with the very components it documents. The <Button> below is the real @halo-ui/react export, rendered inline.

tsx 
import { Button } from '@halo-ui/react'

export function Save() {
  return <Button tone="brand">Save changes</Button>
}

Install

Halo UI is distributed as a set of scoped packages on npm. Install the React bindings and the token layer together.

bash
pnpm add @halo-ui/react @halo-ui/tokens
bash
npm install @halo-ui/react @halo-ui/tokens
bash
yarn add @halo-ui/react @halo-ui/tokens

Import the token stylesheet once at the root of your app. It defines every CSS custom property the components read from.

src/main.tsxtsx
import '@halo-ui/tokens/halo.css'
import { ThemeProvider } from '@halo-ui/react'

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="system">
    <App />
  </ThemeProvider>,
)

Zero-config theming

Components never hard-code color or spacing. Wrap your tree in ThemeProvider and the entire system flips between light, dark, and the high-contrast theme with a single attribute on <html>.

How the system is layered

Halo UI is intentionally split so teams can adopt only what they need.

  1. Tokens — @halo-ui/tokens is the source of truth. Raw values (indigo/600, space/4) compile to CSS variables and a JS/TS object.
  2. Primitives — unstyled, fully accessible behavior (focus management, keyboard nav, ARIA) shared across frameworks.
  3. Components — the styled React layer most product teams consume.
  4. Patterns — opinionated compositions (forms, empty states, page shells) documented as recipes.

Versioning & support

We follow semantic versioning. Token names are treated as public API — a rename is always a major release. The current line is 2.4.0, released 2026-06-09. The previous major (1.x) receives security fixes through the end of 2026.
